what: Event recurrence as a table: which occurrences a set of events (series, the overrides of single occurrences, plain events) yields inside a range. `expect` is what the calendar views and the widget get from shared/recurrence.ts expandAll (rrule.js). Where the reminder path in host-core (expand_occurrences on the rrule crate, one event at a time as event_triggers calls it) answers differently, the row carries that answer as `reminders` and says `surfacesDiffer`. Measured on the real code of both before the port; rows whose note names a decision were changed or added by hand after it.
why: The views and the reminders expand the same series with two libraries in two languages, and the survey of 2026-09-14 found them apart. One expander in the core answers both, and a frontend that is not JavaScript. Every row where the two differ is a decision for the port.
writtenBy: src/intl/eventOccurrences.measure.test.ts — a one-off, run once and deleted: expandAll on every case.
crates/host-core/src/reminders_measure.rs — a one-off, run once and deleted: every case expanded the way event_triggers does, merged in where the instants differ.
Measured twice: the review of PR #67 found gaps, and the second run added the rows it asked for and dropped the emission order from the comparison.

Stage 2 of DESIGN-series-time-zone.md (2026-09-14): a-zone-with-surrounding-space and a-lowercase-zone changed, and four zone rows added, by hand to cal_core::series_clock (decision 26a). Checked by both contract tests, not measured.
readBy: crates/host-core/src/reminders.rs, tests::event_occurrence_contract (the reminders: expand_occurrences, one event at a time)

whereItLives.note: In shared/contracts, beside the other tables both languages check themselves against, because host-core reads it and may embed only from here (KNOWN_REACHES in crates/host-plugins/tests/manifest_reach.rs). When the rule moves into cal-core the table moves beside taskOccurrences.json and host-core stops reading it.

notInThisTable.reminder offsets and the fire window: which reminder fires when (relative offsets, the all-day anchor, catch-up) is host-core’s trigger logic around the expansion; the range here bounds occurrence STARTS on both sides
notInThisTable.the local SQL read: which columns the local reminder path reads is host-core’s (PR #66 adds rrule_tzid); the table starts at the recurrence the path hands on
notInThisTable.the emission order: expandAll sorts its output by the start TEXT (a plain event’s spelling against an occurrence’s .000Z), the reminders sort nothing that matters; the table records occurrences by instant and then input index, so order never counts as a difference
notInThisTable.ids: the occurrence id (`master@ISO`), `series_id`, `occurrence_start` and the `::rid::` override id are the shell’s encoding; the answer here is which input event and which instant
notInThisTable.writing rules: parseRRule, buildRRule, truncateRRuleBefore, splitRRuleForEdit and seriesSplit write or cut rules; they get tables of their own
notInThisTable.the EWS instance index: adapter-ews expands in UTC without exceptions on purpose to count an InstanceIndex — a provider convention, neither a view nor a reminder
notInThisTable.birthdays: yearly all-day events synthesised without a rule (host-core birthdays.rs)
notInThisTable.providers that expand for us: Graph’s calendarView and the device calendars deliver occurrences; nothing is expanded for them

shape.input: {events: [{id, start, end, all_day?, recurrence: {rrule, exceptions, tzid?} | null, cancelled?}], range: {start, end}}; instants in RFC 3339, UTC. `all_day` reads as false when absent; an all-day series repeats on the DEVICE's calendar days (48a) and cancels by the day an exception falls on, so its rows only mean what they say when the reader is in `measuredWith.machineZone`
shape.expect: [{event: index into events, start}], sorted by instant and then by input index
shape.reminders: present only where the reminder path answered differently: the same shape and order, each event expanded on its own (a cancelled event skipped, overrides not applied)
shape.wasTypeScript: a row pinning a JavaScript artifact the port may decide against; it must then change the row on purpose, with a note
shape.instants: compare as instants, never as text: expandAll writes milliseconds (.000Z)
shape.measuredWith: the rrule.js version and the zone of the machine the views’ answer was measured on (the expander does not read it)

cases.name: every-other-week-with-the-week-starting-on-sunday
cases.note: EWS writes WKST whenever Outlook’s week does not start on Monday. With the week starting on Sunday, the Tuesdays are May 5 and 19.

cases.name: every-other-week-with-the-week-starting-on-monday
cases.note: The same rule with the week starting on Monday: the Tuesdays are May 12 and 26.

cases.name: monthly-on-the-last-day
cases.note: A negative day counts from the end of the month.

cases.name: yearly-on-the-first-friday-of-march
cases.note: The yearly form the editor writes (buildRRule).

cases.name: a-start-with-milliseconds
cases.note: The views carry the milliseconds onto every occurrence. The reminders drop the milliseconds and start a day later: their three occurrences are May 2 to 4.

cases.name: a-lowercase-rule
cases.note: rrule.js reads property names in any case.

cases.name: a-trailing-semicolon
cases.note: rrule.js rejects the empty property after the last semicolon (“Unknown RRULE property ''”), and the views show only the master. The reminders read the rule despite the semicolon and expand it.

cases.name: a-start-off-its-listed-weekday
cases.note: The master starts on a Wednesday, the rule lists Mondays. The views do not count the master’s own start: the first occurrence is the Monday after it.

cases.name: a-count-counts-an-excluded-occurrence
cases.note: COUNT includes the excluded occurrence: three are generated and one is removed.

cases.name: a-count-of-zero
cases.note: No occurrence at all, not even the master.

cases.name: an-until-and-a-count-together
cases.note: RFC 5545 forbids both in one rule; rrule.js stops at whichever comes first.

cases.name: a-rule-that-cannot-be-read-keeps-the-master
cases.note: The master is outside the range and is still returned.

cases.name: an-empty-rule-is-no-recurrence
cases.note: The master is outside the range and is still returned: an empty rule is no recurrence.

cases.name: a-plain-event-outside-the-range-passes-through
cases.note: The range bounds expanded occurrences only; the views filter plain events themselves.

cases.name: both-range-ends-are-inclusive
cases.note: Occurrences sit exactly on both ends and both are kept.

cases.name: an-occurrence-that-began-before-the-range
cases.note: Two hours long, starting an hour before the range and still running inside it. Occurrences are chosen by their start, so it is not returned.

cases.name: a-zoned-series-on-both-range-ends-into-summer
cases.note: Monday 09:00 Europe/Berlin; the range starts on the winter occurrence and ends on the summer one. Both ends are kept.

cases.name: a-zoned-series-on-both-range-ends-into-winter
cases.note: Monday 09:00 Europe/Berlin; the range starts on the summer occurrence and ends on the winter one. Both ends are kept.

cases.name: a-zoned-series-near-the-range-end-on-the-change-day
cases.note: Daily 02:30 summer time Europe/Berlin; the range ends 40 minutes after the occurrence on the day the clocks go back. That occurrence is kept.

cases.name: a-zoned-occurrence-just-past-the-range-end
cases.note: The same series; the range ends ten minutes before the second occurrence, and only the first is returned.

cases.name: the-editors-until-on-a-timed-series
cases.note: buildRRule always writes UNTIL at 23:59:59 UTC; read as that instant, May 3 is kept.

cases.name: a-date-only-until-without-a-zone
cases.note: rrule.js reads a date-only UNTIL as 00:00 UTC of that day, so the 09:00 occurrence on May 3 is cut. The rrule crate does not accept the rule with this UNTIL, so the reminders keep only the master.

cases.name: a-date-only-until-on-a-zoned-series
cases.note: 09:00 Europe/Berlin. The views iterate in wall-clock time and read the date as 00:00 local, so May 3 is cut. The rrule crate does not accept the rule with this UNTIL, so the reminders keep only the master.

cases.name: a-date-only-until-on-a-zoned-series-at-one-in-the-morning
cases.note: 01:00 Europe/Berlin, which is 23:00 UTC the day before: a date read as local midnight and one read as UTC midnight give different answers here. The views read it as local midnight and cut May 3. The rrule crate does not accept the rule with this UNTIL, so the reminders keep only the master.

cases.name: an-until-without-z
cases.note: An UNTIL without Z reads as UTC, and 09:00 on May 3 is kept. The rrule crate does not accept the rule with this UNTIL, so the reminders keep only the master.

cases.name: an-until-without-z-on-a-zoned-series
cases.note: 09:00 Europe/Berlin. Only an UNTIL with Z is moved into wall-clock time; one without Z is compared as wall-clock time, so 09:00 local on May 3 is kept. The rrule crate does not accept the rule with this UNTIL, so the reminders keep only the master.

cases.name: an-until-without-z-before-the-wall-clock-time
cases.note: 09:00 Europe/Berlin with UNTIL at 08:00 and no Z: 08:00 as wall clock is before the occurrence, 08:00 UTC is after it. The views compare it as wall-clock time and cut May 3. The rrule crate does not accept the rule with this UNTIL, so the reminders keep only the master.

cases.name: an-until-with-z-on-a-zoned-series-at-its-last-occurrence
cases.note: 09:00 Europe/Berlin; UNTIL is the last occurrence’s instant, moved into wall-clock time and kept.

cases.name: the-editors-until-on-a-zoned-series-late-in-the-evening
cases.note: Daily 00:30 Europe/Berlin (22:30 UTC the day before) with the editor’s UNTIL. Read as an instant, it keeps 00:30 on May 4, local time.

cases.name: a-zoned-until-with-z-across-the-autumn-change
cases.note: Monday 09:00 Europe/Berlin from summer, cut one second before the November 2 occurrence: the rule a “this and all following” split leaves behind. The cut is moved into the zone at its own instant, so the series stops before November 2.

cases.name: a-zoned-until-with-z-across-the-spring-change
cases.note: Monday 09:00 Europe/Berlin from winter, cut one second before the April 6 occurrence; the series stops before April 6.

cases.name: an-until-before-the-start
cases.note: No occurrence, not even the master. The rrule crate does not accept an UNTIL before the start, so the reminders keep the master where the views show nothing.

cases.name: an-all-day-series-west-of-utc-until-its-local-day
cases.note: All-day in New York, read on a device in Berlin: the stored instant is 04:00 UTC. truncateRRuleBefore writes the local day as a date-only UNTIL for an all-day split, so May 6 is meant to be the last day. The views read the date as 00:00 UTC and lose May 6. The rrule crate does not accept a date-only UNTIL on a named clock, so the reminders keep only the master — as before 48a, which changed WHICH clock the series is read on, not what the crate accepts.

cases.name: a-date-only-until-on-an-all-day-series-east-of-utc
cases.note: All-day in Berlin from May 4 (local midnight is 22:00 UTC the day before), with the date-only UNTIL an all-day split writes: May 6 is meant to be the last day. The views read the date as 00:00 UTC, which is 02:00 on May 6 in Berlin, and keep May 6 as the last day. The rrule crate does not accept a date-only UNTIL, so the reminders keep only the master.

cases.name: the-editors-until-on-an-all-day-series-east-of-utc
cases.note: The same Berlin all-day series ended through the editor, which writes UNTIL=20260506T235959Z for “ends on May 6” whether or not the series is all-day. Read as an instant, that is 01:59 on May 7 in Berlin, and May 7 is kept as a fourth day.

cases.name: an-exception-removes-its-occurrence
cases.note: Exceptions match by the exact instant.

cases.name: an-exception-a-millisecond-off-keeps-the-occurrence
cases.note: Exceptions match by the exact instant, to the millisecond. The reminders do not tell the two instants apart and drop the occurrence.

cases.name: an-exception-on-a-zoned-series-at-its-winter-instant
cases.note: Monday 09:00 Europe/Berlin; the excluded Monday is after the clocks change and is written at its winter instant (08:00 UTC).

cases.name: an-exception-at-the-summer-instant-after-the-change-misses
cases.note: The same exception written at the summer instant (07:00 UTC) matches no occurrence.

cases.name: a-zoned-weekly-series-keeps-its-wall-clock-into-winter
cases.note: Monday 09:00 Europe/Berlin: 07:00 UTC in summer, 08:00 UTC in winter.

cases.name: a-zoned-weekly-series-keeps-its-wall-clock-into-summer
cases.note: Monday 09:00 Europe/Berlin: 08:00 UTC in winter, 07:00 UTC in summer.

cases.name: a-wall-clock-in-the-spring-gap
cases.note: Daily 02:30 Europe/Berlin; on 2026-03-29 the clock jumps from 02:00 to 03:00. The views move the missing 02:30 forward by the length of the gap, to 03:30 summer time (01:30 UTC).

cases.name: a-wall-clock-in-the-autumn-overlap
cases.note: Daily 02:30 Europe/Berlin; on 2026-10-25 the clock reads 02:30 twice. The views take the earlier reading, summer time (00:30 UTC).

cases.name: an-unknown-zone
cases.note: An unknown zone expands in UTC.

cases.name: a-zone-named-utc
cases.note: Expands in UTC.

cases.name: an-empty-zone
cases.note: An empty zone is no zone: UTC.

cases.name: a-zone-with-surrounding-space
cases.note: Nothing is trimmed: tzdata does not know the name with the spaces, so the series repeats in UTC in the views and in the reminders alike (cal_core::series_clock). Until 2026-09-14 the reminders trimmed the name and kept the Berlin wall clock.

cases.name: a-lowercase-zone
cases.note: tzdata names match in any ASCII case, so the views and the reminders both keep the Berlin wall clock (cal_core::series_clock). Until 2026-09-14 the reminders knew names only in their exact case and expanded in UTC.

cases.name: a-series-stored-as-etc-utc
cases.note: What Exchange stores for its own UTC. A UTC name, so the series repeats in UTC and 07:00 UTC stays 07:00 UTC across the change in late October. Until 2026-09-14 the views took the zoned path for it, at the same instants; which path a UTC name takes is pinned by crates/cal-core/tests/fixtures/seriesClock.json.

cases.name: a-series-stored-as-gmt
cases.note: GMT is a link to Etc/GMT: zero offset, no daylight saving, a UTC name. The row pins the instants only: zero offset gives the same ones on the zoned path, so which path a UTC name takes is pinned by crates/cal-core/tests/fixtures/seriesClock.json.

cases.name: a-lowercase-utc-name
cases.note: etc/utc is Etc/UTC in any ASCII case, and a UTC name. The row pins the instants only: zero offset gives the same ones on the zoned path, so which path a UTC name takes is pinned by crates/cal-core/tests/fixtures/seriesClock.json.

cases.name: an-offset-for-a-zone-name
cases.note: Sunday 23:30 UTC, weekly on Sundays, stored with the zone +05:30. Intl accepts an offset as a zone: on its clock the start is Monday 05:00 and the Sundays fall a day earlier. tzdata has no such name, so the series repeats in UTC on Sundays, in the views and in the reminders alike (cal_core::series_clock, decided 2026-09-14).

cases.name: a-windows-zone-name
cases.note: EWS maps Windows names to IANA before they get here; a name that slipped through is unknown and expands in UTC.

cases.name: a-fixed-offset-zone
cases.note: Etc/GMT-2 is two hours ahead of UTC all year, so nothing shifts.

cases.name: a-monthly-series-in-new-york-authored-in-winter
cases.note: Second Sunday 19:00 America/New_York, written in December and seen in July: 23:00 UTC on Sunday the 12th.

cases.name: a-daily-series-across-a-change-at-midnight
cases.note: Daily 00:30 America/Santiago, where the clocks change at midnight in early September. The views keep 00:30 local on both sides. On 2026-09-06 the clocks go from 00:00 to 01:00, so 00:30 does not exist that day. The views move it to 01:30; the reminders skip the day and, still counting fourteen, end a day later on 2026-09-13.

cases.name: an-all-day-series-without-zone-into-winter
cases.note: All-day weekly from Monday 2026-10-19 in Berlin, stored as local midnight (22:00 UTC the day before), across the change to winter time on 2026-10-25. An all-day series repeats on the DEVICE's calendar days (48a), so every occurrence is the local midnight of its own Monday: 22:00 UTC before the change, 23:00 UTC after it. Read in UTC, as Aperio read it until now, every later occurrence sat at 23:00 on the SUNDAY — the day before the one the rule names.

cases.name: an-all-day-series-into-summer-keeps-its-monday
cases.note: The same series across the change to summer time on 2027-03-28: Monday 2027-03-22 is local midnight at 23:00 UTC the day before, Monday 2027-03-29 at 22:00 UTC. Both are Mondays on the device's calendar, which is what an all-day series repeats on (48a).

cases.name: an-all-day-exception-cancels-the-day-it-names
cases.note: An all-day Monday series in Berlin, each occurrence at local midnight (22:00 UTC the day before), with 2026-06-15 cancelled — written as midnight UTC, the way a provider that anchors a date elsewhere writes it. A series of days cancels the DAY the exception falls on (48a, decision 95); compared as an instant it would cancel nothing and the deleted day would come back.

cases.name: an-all-day-series-a-provider-gave-a-zone
cases.note: An all-day series is read on the device's days whatever zone it carries: the same Berlin Mondays, with a zone fourteen hours ahead written onto the series. A zone does harm on the wire (46a) and changes nothing here.

cases.name: a-moved-occurrence-stands-in-for-its-slot
cases.note: The override’s id names the series and the slot it replaces. The views drop the master’s slot and show the override at its new time. The reminders expand each event on its own and apply no override: the master’s slot fires as well as the override.

cases.name: a-cancelled-occurrence-removes-its-slot
cases.note: The views drop the master’s slot and the cancelled override both. The reminders skip the cancelled override and still fire at the master’s slot.

cases.name: a-moved-occurrence-of-a-zoned-series-after-the-change
cases.note: Monday 09:00 Europe/Berlin from summer; CalDAV names the slot of the November 2 occurrence by its winter instant. The views drop that slot and show the override at 12:00 UTC. The reminders apply no override: the November 2 slot fires as well as the override.

cases.name: an-override-without-its-series
cases.note: Shown as it is.

cases.name: an-override-for-a-slot-the-rule-never-makes
cases.note: No slot of the master matches, so the views show every occurrence of the rule and the override.

cases.name: an-override-slot-in-another-spelling
cases.note: The slot is written with an offset instead of Z and matched as an instant. The reminders apply no override: the master’s slot fires as well as the override.

cases.name: an-override-slot-that-is-not-an-instant
cases.note: No slot to drop: the views show the override beside every occurrence of the master.

cases.name: a-cancelled-override-slot-that-is-not-an-instant
cases.note: The cancelled override is dropped, and every occurrence of the master stays.

cases.name: an-override-listed-before-its-series
cases.note: The order of the list does not matter for which slot is dropped. The reminders apply no override: the master’s slot fires as well as the override.

cases.name: a-cancelled-series
cases.note: A whole cancelled series, no override id. The views keep it; whether it is shown is the show-cancelled setting’s business. The reminders skip a cancelled event entirely: a cancelled meeting never nags.

cases.name: two-series-at-the-same-instant
cases.note: Equal instants are recorded by input index; the order expandAll emits is not part of the table.

cases.name: a-plain-event-at-the-same-instant-as-an-occurrence
cases.note: The plain event is listed first. expandAll would emit the occurrence first (its start text ends in .000Z); the table records both at the same instant, by input index.

cases.name: a-long-daily-series-in-a-wide-range
cases.note: Daily for eighteen months. The views have no cap. The reminders stop at 500 occurrences (RRULESET_LIMIT).
